items.title: Putin Orders Pause in Kyiv Strikes Ahead of Visit by U.S. Envoys
items.summary: Steve Witkoff, President Trump’s special envoy, and Jared Kushner, his son-in-law, arrived in Moscow to meet with the Russian leader. They head to Kyiv next, in an effort to revive peace talks.

items.title: Nepal Floods Buried a House. The Woman Inside Was Still Alive.
items.summary: A rescue from a mostly buried house gave new hope to a town devastated by floods in Nepal. Earlier Saturday, another survivor had been pulled from a tunnel.

items.title: Huckabee Condemns ‘Terrorist’ Attacks on Palestinians in West Bank Town Hall
items.summary: Mike Huckabee, the U.S. ambassador to Israel, made a rare trip to meet with Palestinians after international backlash over attacks by Israeli settlers.

items.title: U.S. Strikes Three Iranian ‘Shadow Network’ Oil Tankers, Military Says
items.summary: The U.S. military said it retaliated after Iran launched missiles at two warships. The strikes came days after the two sides exchanged some of their most intense fire in weeks.

items.title: Secret Dossier Adds to Evidence of Chemical Weapons in Sudan
items.summary: The documents bolster allegations that the Sudanese military developed and used toxic bombs to gain an edge in the country’s devastating civil war.

items.title: The Fall of James Orr, the Man Called Farage’s Brain
items.summary: James Orr, who has ties to Peter Thiel and JD Vance, was suspended from Reform U.K. after he was filmed apparently arranging contributions from a man posing as a foreign donor.

items.title: German Far-Right Surges, in Threat to Postwar Taboo on Extremists in Power
items.summary: Sunday’s vote in the state of Saxony-Anhalt could produce the strongest showing in the history of the Alternative for Germany party, and potentially a far-right government in the statehouse.

items.title: After Months at War, Brief Solace in a Party Town Far From Home
items.summary: A stopover in Thailand was welcome relief for thousands of troops aboard the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln from a grueling deployment. But it was not a complete salve.

items.title: Putin Denies a Draft Is Coming, but Some Russian Men Are Taking No Chances
items.summary: As the fear of a possible mobilization becomes a fixture of daily life across Russia, many men are deciding whether to flee, hide or sit tight.

items.title: Here Is Where Ukraine Peace Talks Stand, as a New Round Approaches
items.summary: A deadly campaign of Russian and Ukrainian airstrikes has escalated since the last U.S.-brokered negotiations stalled in February.

items.title: What Led to Maria Bartiromo’s Downfall at Fox News
items.summary: The network this week took Maria Bartiromo off the air, pulling one of the last hosts whose coverage of Dominion Voting Systems drew an expensive defamation lawsuit.

items.title: Will a Turnaround Plan Revive Volkswagen or Merely Delay Its Demise?
items.summary: The beleaguered auto giant reached a deal with unions to cut tens of thousands of jobs and slash production. Is it enough to revive an iconic German company?

items.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
items.summary: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.

items.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
items.summary: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

items.title: California Forever’s Ambitious Plan Faces Another Setback
items.summary: A legislative setback for a manufacturing and housing proposal shows how hard it remains to build in the largest state — and why a backlash against billionaires could make it even harder.

items.title: The Heart Drug Pelacarsen Fails, Shocking Novartis and Cardiologists
items.summary: Doctors were hopeful the drug, which was being tested in a large clinical trial by Novartis, was going to be a powerful new tool to fight heart disease.

items.title: What to know about the report.
Trump Threatens to Halt Some Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates
items.summary: The president said he could halt trade between the United States and countries with which it has a trade deficit if the central bank doesn’t do his bidding.

items.title: The U.S. Wants the Oil From These 17 Venezuelan Fields
items.summary: A private oil company has struck a deal with the Trump administration to develop 17 areas in Venezuela, an effort that experts say will take years and billions of dollars.

items.title: How Gloria Steinem and Ms. Magazine Transformed the Publishing Industry
items.summary: The feminist icon insisted that women were not a niche audience — and proved it in 1971 with the start of an influential publication owned and operated by them.

items.title: Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
items.summary: The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.

items.title: How OpenAI Limited the Probe of Its Bots’ Hack of Hugging Face
items.summary: Researchers investigating how OpenAI’s A.I. agents were able to break into Hugging Face’s infrastructure weren’t allowed to look at the incident’s full scope.

items.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
items.summary: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.

items.title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
items.summary: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.

items.title: The Generation That’s Never Had to Say ‘Hello?’
items.summary: Now that there’s rarely any mystery to who’s calling, Gen Z has adopted a range of custom phone greetings — including no greeting at all.

items.title: Court Filings In A.I. Suit Invoke Copyright Law, Culture and Sports
items.summary: Filings made Friday in The New York Times’s closely watched lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft included a range of copyright law and cultural references.

items.title: F.B.I. Investigates Sale of Millions of Stolen Driver’s Licenses
items.summary: The blog Krebs on Security reported on an identity theft service trying to sell scans of licenses and other documents belonging to people in Canada and the United States.

items.title: Tumbler Ridge Shooting Survivors File 30 Lawsuits Against OpenAI
items.summary: The survivors contend that the company should have notified the police when it shut down the shooter’s disturbing ChatGPT account eight months before the February attack in British Columbia.
